artworks.title: The Laestrygonians Hurl Rocks at the Fleet (Odyssey Landscapes)
artworks.description: From the oldest surviving painted cycle of the Odyssey, dug from a house on the Esquiline: the giants tear boulders from the cliffs while the ships below are speared like fish.

artworks.title: Circe Offering the Cup to Ulysses
artworks.description: Enthroned between drugged swine and scattered herbs, the goddess lifts cup and wand at once — and in the bronze mirror behind her, small and armed, stands the man the drug will not touch.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Camerini's peplum keeps Aeolus' bag and Circe's cup — the opened winds and the men turned to swine.

films.title: The Odyssey
films.description: The miniseries gives Circe her year on Aeaea — Hermes' moly, the swine, and the road to the underworld.

popCulture.title: Circe
popCulture.creator: Madeline Miller
popCulture.description: Miller retells Aeaea from the witch's side — the cup, the exile, and Odysseus as one visitor among many.

popCulture.title: Odyssey
popCulture.description: Book X — Aeolus' bag opened, the Laestrygonian harbour, and Circe's island before the Nekuia.

popCulture.title: Circe
popCulture.description: The daughter of Helios who turns sailors to beasts — and then points the way to the dead.
